public_rationale: Pew observed Google AI summaries in results collected April 7–17, 2025, supporting the search-output component [e1]. Google's July 29, 2026 announcement describes organizational features but does not measure dependable performance [e2]. ORO's October 2026 evaluation found that 73 of 235 assistant-task pairs that passed at least once failed on another attempt, with up to five attempts per task [e3]. This evidence does not establish dependable life organization in repeated practical use, so the two-part forecast remains unresolved [e1, e2, e3].
limitations: Pew did not directly grade the summaries' writing quality or factual reliability [e1].
Google's announcement does not independently verify successful task completion [e2].
The repeated-task results do not establish dependable management across a person's schedules, tasks and everyday arrangements [e3].
The packet establishes neither that no qualifying agent exists nor that either capability is impossible [e1, e2, e3].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Search engines that return well-written paragraphs and AI agents that can organize lives will eventually arrive, though possibly only for our grandchildren or their children.
conditions: possibly only in the time of our grandchildren or their children

statement.excerpt: We will eventually see search engines that return neatly written paragraphs, and eventually see AI agents that can organize lives. Or at least our grandchildren or their children will.
statement.document_title: Why driverless cars might—or might not—be at the end of the road

from_speaker: search engines that return neatly written paragraphs
AI agents that can organize lives
Or at least our grandchildren or their children will
our_interpretation: The claim forecasts two capabilities. Establishing only one does not settle the whole claim.
I read 'neatly written paragraphs' as coherent, readable prose answers to searches. Marcus supplies no writing-quality measure.

I read 'organize lives' as practical, dependable help managing schedules, tasks and everyday arrangements. User direction and approval are compatible with this reading; perfect performance and complete autonomy are not required.
The surrounding discussion makes reliability relevant, but Marcus specifies neither a success rate nor how broadly an agent must operate.
The reference to descendants allows a long wait. It supplies neither a calendar deadline nor an antecedent that must occur before scoring.
I do not add a requirement for universal adoption or a particular AI architecture.
criteria.support_condition: Publicly accessible search engines demonstrably produce coherent prose answers, and available AI agents demonstrably manage a range of ordinary personal arrangements dependably in repeated practical use.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Decisive evidence establishes that at least one promised capability cannot arrive. Present limitations or elapsed time alone cannot contradict an eventual forecast without a deadline.

evidence.locator: Findings on AI-summary frequency and length; methodology dates result collection to April 7–17, 2025
evidence.explanation: Directly observed prose-length search summaries support the search-output component. Length alone does not establish writing quality or the stronger interpretation of consistently reliable answers.

evidence.locator: Opening description, following the school-email and permission-slip example
evidence.explanation: Google describes an agent for organizational chores, including school-email deadlines, itineraries and calendar arrangements. These advertised capabilities are relevant progress, but the announcement does not measure successful completion or reliability.

evidence.excerpt: 31% of tasks passed once were failed on another try.
evidence.explanation: The evaluation reports successful everyday task execution alongside inconsistent repeated performance; its detailed denominator is assistant-task pairs that succeeded at least once. Its small, simulated task set does not establish dependable life organization, and failures cannot contradict eventual arrival.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Dated observations of coherent prose search answers, together with repeated practical evaluations showing an available agent dependably managing schedules, tasks and everyday arrangements, would support the forecast. Evaluations should record failures and human intervention. Decisive evidence that either capability cannot arrive would contradict it; continued delay alone would not.
